summary: Standardized custom RFID cards for vibe-coding projects: a tray-printing ID card app, a 3D-printable RFID reader enclosure, and the Wish It Better framework.
origin: Not a git fork (GitHub reports fork=false), and not original either. The enclosure is the published tip of a pre-git parametric-model line in a local fab-lab workspace that predates this repo by about ten weeks: hardware/rfid-reader-case/gen_rfid_reader_case_v7.py records in its own header that it carries the tongue-and-groove-plus-bead seal and the mid-plane clamshell split from kunai_360_onex_v4.py -- the model line later published as KUNAI-001 on this same registry -- and adopts pearl_box_v2_voxel_v4.py's gyroid cell clamp verbatim -- "Orin drawer" is v7's own name for that upstream, which never uses the phrase (grep -c -i orin returns 12 in v7 and 0 in the file it names). So the two hardware projects listed here are siblings out of one Pearl Box voxel/gyroid fab method that has never been published and is on no wish-it-better manifest. This sentence read "appears in no repo" for four commits and that was false -- one of the two files named above is tracked in a private repository, which is deliberately not named here, because naming it would publish a private thing in order to correct a public sentence. src/web/vendor/qr.js states at line 22 that its structure and tables derive from Project Nayuki's QR Code generator (MIT). The Wish It Better spec this project defines was copied into the nested-resonance-memory-archive repo, making two other listed entries downstream of this one. Fragment-Mono and Instrument Serif (SIL OFL 1.1, see OFL.txt) are embedded in src/site/gt/.
amended: v1.0.1 — §1/§4: the account-free route is the minimum, not the issue tracker
_note: Level is L0, CORRECTED DOWN FROM L1 ON 2026-08-19, and the sentence that did the inflating is struck by name rather than edited out, because a reader who saw it deserves to learn it is gone. It read: 'Level is L1.' It stood from this repo's second commit (d2fbaac, 2026-08-09) and nothing was ever measured under it. Section 3's L1 row is L0 + every shipped change carries an eval meeting section 2 + wishes reach a terminal state. The third clause holds and is measured: every wish this project has received reached shipped or declined (tools/wishing_well.py --stats, 2026-08-19: VIBE-CARDS-001 19 shipped + 7 declined, 0 new, 0 building). The second clause does not hold, and section 5 says where to look: 'Git history is the ledger ... the commits, the issue that caused them, the eval that proved them.' Every one of the 179 commits shipped since L1 was declared was read in full on 2026-08-19 (message plus diffstat, six readers against one written rubric, recorded in docs/EVALS.md section 6): 113 carry an eval meeting section 2 — a failing condition written down AND a check at the artifact, or a gate added that fails on regression of that change; 45 carry a measurement but no written failing condition, or a check only at the source; 21 carry neither — two of those have no body at all (9adbf8b, a one-line CSS change; 9c5ee6d, one manifest field). So 66 of 179 shipped changes, 37 percent, do not meet the bar, and 'every' fails on the first of them. The other evidence points the same way: docs/EVALS.md, the file this manifest names under `evals`, had six entries and had last been touched on 2026-08-17 (b3eef58) when this was read, so no shipped change in between had added to it; the PR-template checklist in section 2 has gated nothing because this repository has had zero pull requests; and this repo's own per-card manifests (src/site/*/wish-it-better.json) already say 'shipped changes here do not carry an eval meeting section 2' — and those card pages are this repo's shipped changes, in this ledger. This is the mirror of the KUNAI-001 correction of 2026-08-14, which stayed at L0 because 'an eval is not a queue'; here a queue is not an eval, and half of two is still not one. The classification is a reading, not a gate: the rubric and every non-EVAL commit are listed in docs/EVALS.md so it can be re-read and disputed. The 21 with neither, oldest last: 9adbf8b c3597fa 50223e4 83ab734 ba70d21 9908da0 b3eef58 66b65c5 1967718 6b0deb0 111611d 2473813 38cbdea 73fc6a5 a3ec93f 6326a9e e3b926c f0908ca b70d95f 9c9fe43 9c5ee6d. THE WAY BACK TO L1 IS WRITE-DISCIPLINE, NOT TOOLING (section 1.3: no new tooling for a behavioural problem): from this commit on, every shipped change states what would have proven it wrong and what was checked at the artifact, in the commit message, which is the ledger; the level moves back up when a re-read of the ledger since this commit finds no shipped change without one, and not before. wish_channel is the wishing well on the landing page, not a mailto: a mailto is account-free but it is not a queue — it has no status, no ordering, and it made a human's inbox the precondition for anything happening. The well needs no account, no mail client and no address, and it lands in a queue an agent works. verify_pages_artifact.mjs proves the declared page actually carries the well rather than trusting the URL. `amended` carries one entry and briefly carried two: the second read "v1.0.2 — origin filled", and `git log -S` puts it in 7f0cb71, a commit that does not touch WISH_IT_BETTER.md at all. The standard records exactly one amendment in force, v1.0.1, so v1.0.2 named a spec change that never happened. §5 defines an amendment as a PR touching WISH_IT_BETTER.md AND adding the project to `amended`; filling a field in this manifest is neither half. It is deleted rather than backfilled with a genuine v1.0.2, because §5's own third rule is to write the deletion first. The reason this is not a changelog tidy: `amended` is the field L2 reads as proof of contributing back, and §5 says even v1.0.1 "earns nobody L2" because the origin project found it — so an entry with no spec change behind it is level inflation on the one file every adopter copies.
